Conclusion: The test `testCommandLineNoDefault` checks whether Luigi's command line parser correctly sets task parameters when no default value is provided in the configuration or command line arguments. However, it failed with a `MissingParameterException`, indicating that the parameter `p_not_global_no_default` was not set even though there was no default value assigned to it.

The issue arises because the test uses the method `run_and_check` which internally calls `luigi.parameter.get_task_parameters`. This function is expected to raise a `MissingParameterException` if a required parameter does not have a provided value or a default value. In this case, since there's no default value assigned to `p_not_global_no_default`, the test should set it explicitly using command line arguments before calling `run_and_check`.

To fix this issue, update the test method as follows:

```python
def testCommandLineNoDefault(self):
    ...
    self.assertTrue(self.run_and_check(['MyClass2', '--p-not-global-no-default', '123']))
```

In the updated version of the test, I've added `'--p-not-global-no-default', '123'` to the arguments passed to `run_and_check` method. This should set the value of `p_not_global_no_default` parameter before calling `luigi.parameter.get_task_parameters`, thereby preventing the `MissingParameterException`.
